newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
NO GLORY ON THE HARBOUR TODAY

The long-awaited Sydney-to-Hobart warm-up clash between Australia's fastest maxi yacht, Brindabella, and her German-owned rival, Morning Glory, won't eventuate in the Canon Big Boat Challenge on Sydney Harbour today.

The Big Boat Challenge has become a traditional sparring contest between the maxis before they slug it out all the way to Hobart but, unfortunately, the bulk of Morning Glory's international crew of 22 won't fly in before the weekend.

"Our main reason for coming to Australia is to win the Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart and, while we would have liked to sail in the Big Boat Challenge, we can't go out with half the crew not aboard," the yacht's captain, New Zealander BARRY MACKAY said today.

Owner HASSO PLATTNER, co-founder of the SAP computer company, is due in Sydney on Saturday. Also arriving over the weekend is one of the two principal helmsmen, Brazilian TORBEN GRAEL, the Star class gold medallist at the Atlanta Games.

Navigator on Morning Glory is Australian ANDREW CAPE, the yacht designer and internationally sought-after navigator who filled this position aboard the U.S. maxi Sayonara when it won last year's Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart.

The absence of Morning Glory means today's Big Boat Challenge will leave Brindabella's main opposition coming from PETER WALKER's just re-keeled Foxtel Amazon and the Whitbread-60, Elle Racing, sailed by ADRIENNE CAHALAN and her all-female crew.
Nevertheless, the Big Boat Challenge will be a great event to watch, with the course taking the fleet twice around Fort Denison and a finish off the Opera House.
AYF NAMES NEW GENERAL MANAGER

After sailing under a jury-rigged helm for more than five months, the Australian Yachting Federation (AYF) has finally appointed a new general manager in the widely-experienced yachting administrator, PHIL JONES.

Of particular importance is that JONES, an Australian who has lived in Britain for some years, was the International Sailing Federation's (ISAF) Olympic Manager and oversaw preparations for the 1996 Olympic yachting regatta at Savannah.

JONES was a staff member of England's Royal Yachting Association (RYA), and was responsible for developing all the current RYA windsurfing programmes before he formed Waterfront Sport Management Ltd, a company specialising in sailing and water sports event management, sponsorship and consultancy.

Among the events Waterfront manages are the Ultra 30 grand prix circuit and Grand Prix Sailing's 18-foot skiff U.K. tour. The ISAF contracted JONES for a variety of activities. He was its race management consultant at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics and managed the involvement of the ISAF at the first World Sailing Championships at La Rochelle, France.

GLENN BOURKE, Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games' (SOCOG) competition manager for sailing, who was a coach with the Australian team at the Olympics, told me yesterday: "Everyone thought he was fantastic.
"He is very knowledgeable, was competitor-orientated and has good people skills.
"His experience will be invaluable in the support he can give to SOCOG in the lead-up to 2000, with so many major regattas to be staged in Australia as well as the Games."
Having seen JONES in action at the daily officials' briefing at Savannah, I certainly agree with BOURKE's assessment of his ability and approach to professional management of the sport of sailing.
LIGHT WINDS FOR TELSTRA CUP
The inaugural Telstra Cup offshore regatta has been plagued by light winds this week, with a two-hour delay on the opening day and three hours on the second day before racing got underway.
The light wind has also had an effect on official functions ashore.

On Wednesday, the first of two 12-nautical mile races on Sydney Harbour did not finish until 4.30 p.m. and Cruising Yacht Club of Australia (CYCA) officials sent the fleet off on a second race at 5 p.m.

Back at the CYCA, CHARLES CURRAN's launching party for his new 60-footer, Sydney, got underway with a few guests still on the water, but over at the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron the host was still at sea for the launching of RAY ROBERT's imported Corel-45, BZW Challenge, when the party began at 5.30 p.m.

ROBERTS, chief executive of Workforce International, along with a talented crew that included JAMIE WILMOT, finally made it back to the Squadron with the sleek-looking 45-footer around eight o'clock to find shorebound guests not standing on ceremony and enjoying the soiree.

Joining CURRAN, who is chairman of Capital Investments, and his designer and boat-building partner IAIN MURRAY, the former America's Cup sailor, were many other prominent yachtie/businessmen, including DENNIS O'NEILL and MARCUS BLACKMORE.
NEW YACHTS HEADING FOR HOBART
Sydney and BZW Challenge are both heading south in the Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart on Boxing Day, with an expected fleet of 94 yachts following the late withdrawal of former winner Zeus II.

Sydney looks impressive but is untried. Her first sail will be in today's Canon Big Boat Challenge on the harbour. She is a pilot house version of the Sydney-60s being built by Bashford International at Nowra, New South Wales.

BZW Challenge, however, came to Australia with an impressive record and is showing her mark in the Telstra Cup. As Beau Geste, the BRUCE FARR-designed 45-footer won the International Measurement System (IMS) racer division of the Big Boat Series in San Francisco in September.
In the Telstra Cup racing she has been snapping at the transoms of Kenwood Cup team winners Ragamuffin and Ausmaid.
With JAMIE WILMOT on the helm she is showing excellent upwind speed and could provide a strong bid for IMS honours in the Hobart race.
OLYMPIC MEDALLIST TO START RACE TO COFFS HARBOUR

COLIN BEASHEL, who went so close to winning the gold medal in the Star class at the Atlanta Olympics, will be official starter for the Strathfield Car Radios Pittwater-to-Coffs Harbour race starting on December 27.

The Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club has received 86 entries for the 225-nautical mile warm water coastal passage north, with many yachts turning out this weekend for the two-race lead-up Marantz Ocean Series off Palm Beach.

Among the entries received for the Coffs Harbour series are Infinity III, the original Brindabella now owned by Sydney solicitor MARTIN JAMES, and the Mumm-36, Sea, which advertising man STEVE KULMAR is using in preparation for an Admiral's Cup team bid next year.
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
